title: Development of an AI-based camera system for quantitative assessment of the upper and lower extremities in the context of return-to-sport/return-to-competition (RTS/RTC) evaluations.
summary:
As part of the project, a camera-based system was developed that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to analyze, among other parameters, joint angles while athletes perform Return to Sport/Competition (RTC)-relevant exercises.
The AI-based evaluation of exercise performance during the examinations represents a substantial time saving and simplification for the examiner. This time efficiency would result in increased examination capacity by freeing up clinical and diagnostic resources.
Furthermore, the simplification of the examination process could enable assessments to be performed by trained assistants, which would further increase examination capacity. Consequently, this could enable significantly improved accessibility to RTC assessments in recreational sports, thereby reducing the risk of re-injury and subsequent injuries.
In professional sports, the objectification associated with AI-based evaluation may counteract performance-pressure–induced premature returns to competition. Even in the absence of a systematic tendency toward early return-to-play decisions, the examiner-independence provided by AI-based assessment represents a fundamental improvement in diagnostic quality and reliability.
conditions: Complex movement of the upper and lower extremities

interventions.name: Automated RTC assessment using an AI-based camera system to analyze joint angles and movement patterns during standardized return-to-sport/competition exercises.
Manual return-to-competition (RTC) assessment using standardized clinical-functional tests and conventional sports medicine evaluations performed by qualified professionals.
